newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:

AMLC COMMENTARY: Australian cattle and sheep markets had a typical winter feel about them this week, featuring a wide price differential between slaughter and store quality stock.

Generally, poor pasture conditions and warnings of another El Nino weather event has increased store stock offerings and, at the same time, made graziers cautious participants in these markets. This has reduced demand for unfinished stock.
Accordingly, prices for store condition stock eased. However, prices improved for the lower numbers of slaughter ready stock. Only forward store condition stock, which attracted the eye of
feedlotters and the odd restocker, broke this trend and held firm.

The lift in values of slaughter cattle has not been solely due to lower supplies. A modest improvement in trading conditions in export markets over the past fortnight, coupled with a lower A$, has improved Australian processor margins and therefore demand for livestock.
Buying by processors successful in the recent Korean tender, lifted medium weight steer prices at saleyards by 4-5c/kg lw across the eastern states and in South Australia.

In the U.S., beef sales over the recent 4th of July holiday weekend were reported to have been very good. This has helped clear inventories and led to solid demand for lean imported beef this week, as end-users endeavour to replenish stock levels.

Demand for imported beef has been supported by the favourable discount it holds in relation to similar U.S. domestic product, lower supplies of U.S. domestic product and reduced offerings out of both Australia and New Zealand.
By week's end, Australian lean manufacturing product was trading from 4-10 Ac/kg higher in the U.S. market. In Australian saleyards, cows generally enjoyed prices rises of around the same magnitude.

However, in the U.S. cuts market, demand was not so strong. Boxed beef values fell 1-3 USc/lb this week and, at 99.26USc/lb, the light choice cutouts are now trading 2USc/lb below last year. U.S. cattle prices also followed this downturn trend slipping 2.4USc/lb to 61.5USc/lb.

On the Japanese market improved beef consumption levels coupled with stronger trade buying to build stocks for the anticipated increase in consumer demand over the Obon holiday period (mid-August), led to a lift in wholesale prices.
Strength in the Japanese wholesale market again translated into higher export prices. Bids for chilled product increased by 17-47Ac/kg FAS, whilst frozen product prices also improved, by 1-13Ac/kg.

Looking forward, manufacturing beef prices should find support from a reduction in supplies from New Zealand and a much lower U.S. cow kill compared with last year. Prices should remain relatively firm until at least the start of the U.S. cow run in October.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
